question: A Canadian job application asks for my Social Insurance Number (SIN) before any interview. Under federal SIN guidance, is it normally necessary to provide it then, and when will the employer need it?
generated_answer: The SIN is a nine-digit number that you will need to work in Canada and to access government programs and benefits. You must give your SIN to your employer within three days of starting your job. If you do not have a SIN, you must apply for one. You can apply for a SIN at a Service Canada Centre. You will need to provide your employer with a copy of your SIN application form. Your employer will need your SIN to report your employment to the Canada Revenue Agency (CRA) and to deduct income tax from your pay. If you do not provide your employer with your SIN, they may not be able to deduct income tax from your pay. This could result in you owing money to the CRA. It is important to note that you should never give your SIN to anyone who does not need it. This includes your employer, unless they are required to have it for tax purposes. If you are unsure about whether or not you need to provide your SIN, you can contact the CRA for more information.
